clue.text: " Bottoms up !" order ?

parts.note: the drinker's toast, read literally, is an instruction to turn something upside down

explanation.surface: A toastmaster calls out the cheery drinking command.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottoms up!' is a toast, but taken literally it orders you to turn a thing so its bottom is on top.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn something upside down is to set its base uppermost, which is what the literal command asks.

clue.text: Use copper nails perhaps it's in sea water

definitions.text: Use copper nails perhaps it's in sea water

parts.words: Use copper nails perhaps it's in sea water
parts.note: copper nails resist the sea, and the thing described is a piece of ground surrounded by the sea

explanation.surface: Advice to a boatbuilder: use copper nails, since the vessel sits in salt water.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is shipbuilding advice, but the clue ends by describing a piece of land with sea all round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A body of land surrounded by water, sitting in the sea.

clue.text: Liquid remedy for a broken crown

definitions.text: Liquid remedy for a broken crown

parts.words: Liquid remedy for a broken crown
parts.note: the nursery rhyme Jack and Jill has Jack, who broke his crown, treat his head with this liquid and brown paper

explanation.surface: Someone asks what will cure a cracked crown.
explanation.walkthrough: In the English nursery rhyme Jack fell down and broke his crown (head), then went to bed to mend his head with vinegar and brown paper; 'crown' looks royal or dental.
explanation.definitionFit: An acidic liquid made from fermented wine or cider, used in the rhyme as a poultice.

clue.text: Replace in military clique ?

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, is a British army corps
a set is a clique or circle of people

explanation.surface: A substitute is found within an army faction.
explanation.definitionFit: To put back in place or set again is to replace.

clue.text: Pardons a sailor's turbulent loves

parts.note: an AB (able seaman) is a sailor; with the 's this gives AB plus S

indicators.note: turbulent means stirred up, so the letters of loves are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A forgiving figure excuses a seaman's stormy love affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a sailor's' looks like a possessive in the surface, but it supplies the able seaman and his S; 'turbulent' is the anagram signal on 'loves'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean to forgive, releasing someone from blame or penalty.

clue.text: Long note from a dumb revenue officer

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A lengthy memo comes from a silent tax inspector.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' takes the run inside 'dumB REVEnue'; 'a' and 'officer' complete the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A breve is a note of long duration, twice a semibreve.

clue.text: Stubborn old boys ate out of a can

parts.note: OBs are old boys, former pupils of a school
a can is a tin; 'out of a' only sets the scene of eating from it
taken as written

explanation.surface: Obstinate former pupils ate straight from the tin.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as boys eating from a can; in the wordplay 'out of a' is only a link, and the pieces join as old boys, can, ate.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe someone who refuses to change their mind, being dogged and unyielding.

clue.text: Boasted of five relative notes

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
an aunt is a relative
E and D are two musical notes

explanation.surface: Someone bragged about five related musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: To vaunt is to boast, so this is something boasted about, praised extravagantly.

clue.text: Do these orders refer to the National Anthem ?

definitions.text: Do these orders refer to the National Anthem ?

parts.words: Do these orders refer to the National Anthem ?
parts.note: people rise to their feet for the anthem, and the phrase for permanent regular instructions begins with the word for being upright

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether certain instructions concern the anthem.
explanation.walkthrough: Standing orders are permanent instructions, or regular bank payments; audiences stand for the National Anthem.
explanation.definitionFit: Upright on one's feet, as for an anthem, and also fixed or permanent as with lasting instructions.

clue.text: Poor, poor Mr. Andersen comes round and catches a whale

indicators.note: comes round means the storyteller's first name encloses the scrambled letters

parts.note: Hans Christian Andersen, the Danish teller of fairy tales

indicators.note: poor means badly made, so the following word's letters are in poor order

explanation.surface: Pity poor Andersen, who encircles and lands a whale.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Poor' is pity in the surface but is the anagram signal on the second 'poor'; 'comes round' puts the storyteller's first name around that result.
explanation.definitionFit: A whaler spears and takes a whale with barbed spears, so the verb means catches by that method.

clue.text: Disembarks at the headland and makes a scene

parts.note: to disembark is to land, so 'disembarks' gives lands
a cape is a headland jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: A traveller steps ashore on a promontory and admires the view.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to lay out grounds or a view is to make a scene of them, as a garden designer does.

clue.text: Bath's sex-appeal girl

parts.note: SA is an old abbreviation for sex appeal
Una is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A city's alluring young woman is described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bath' looks like the English spa city, but it is the definition; the 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A sauna is a steam bath of Finnish origin.

clue.text: "Brief as the lightning in the collied" (M. N. Dream)

definitions.text: "Brief as the lightning in the collied" (M. N. Dream)

parts.words: "Brief as the lightning in the collied" (M. N. Dream)
parts.note: a quotation from A Midsummer ... Dream with its last word left blank for the solver to supply

explanation.surface: A line of Shakespeare is quoted with its final word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Lysander's line in A Midsummer Night's Dream reads 'Brief as the lightning in the collied night'; 'collied' means blackened, as with coal.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word completes Lysander's line about darkness as black as coal.

clue.text: Porto Rico proclamation the journalist foretold

parts.note: PR is the abbreviation for Puerto Rico, once spelt Porto Rico
an edict is an official proclamation
ED, short for editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A newspaperman anticipated an official announcement from the Caribbean island.
explanation.definitionFit: To foretell something is to predict it, saying beforehand what will happen.

clue.text: Magical word of music

explanation.surface: A conjuror's utterance doubles as a musical direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Conjurors say 'hey presto' as the trick completes, and in a score the Italian marking means play very fast.

clue.text: The diamond game

explanation.surface: A precious stone is also a pastime.
explanation.definitionFit: A single gem set alone in a ring is called this, and so is a card or peg game played by one person.

clue.text: Rejoice, with a learned cleric in the valley

indicators.note: in places the cleric and the article inside the word for valley

parts.note: a glen is a narrow valley, especially in Scotland
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a learned clergyman

explanation.surface: A scholarly priest down in the dale finds happiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal. 'Rejoice' here is the transitive sense, to make someone glad, which fits the answer as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Used transitively, to rejoice someone is to delight them, to make them happy.

clue.text: Soldier takes artist only a stone

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
sole means only

explanation.surface: A soldier takes an artist just one pebble.
explanation.definitionFit: A girasole is a fire opal, a gemstone that shows a glowing light.

clue.text: How to win a ballet competition?

definitions.text: How to win a ballet competition?

parts.words: How to win a ballet competition?
parts.note: a boxing victory decided by the judges' scores, applied to dancers who balance on their toe tips

explanation.surface: Someone asks how one triumphs in a dance contest.
explanation.walkthrough: A boxer may win on points rather than by a knockout; ballerinas dance on points, on the tips of their toes.
explanation.definitionFit: Winning by judges' score rather than knockout, and dancing on the tips of the toes.

clue.text: They are associated with rash piques

explanation.surface: Something tied to hasty acts also irritates people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rash' suggests hastiness, but it is the skin rash: nettle rash is the British name for hives.
explanation.definitionFit: Stinging plants of this kind cause nettle rash, and as a verb the word means annoys or irritates.

clue.text: Examples of needlework on tambours perhaps

definitions.text: Examples of needlework on tambours perhaps

parts.words: Examples of needlework on tambours perhaps
parts.note: needle designs inked into skin, and drumbeats played on drums, a tambour being both a drum and an embroidery hoop

explanation.surface: Embroidery stitched on a round frame.
explanation.walkthrough: A tambour is an embroidery frame but also a drum, and drummed signals are also called by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: Designs pricked into skin with a needle, and drum signals beaten out, as at a military display.

clue.text: Right! He's with us, the monkey !

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone cheerfully confirms that the primate has joined the group.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhesus macaque is an Asian monkey, which gave its name to the Rh blood factor.

clue.text: Going down ?Not these edifying influences

parts.note: influences that raise the spirit cannot be going down, since they lift people upward

explanation.surface: Morally improving forces are not in decline.
explanation.walkthrough: Things that raise you morally go up, not down, the opposite of 'Going down'.
explanation.definitionFit: Influences that raise morale or improve people morally, literally lifting them up.

clue.text: Intervals when the odds are on the experts

indicators.note: are on places the odds above the experts in this down entry

parts.note: SP is the starting price, the betting odds at the start of a race
aces are experts

explanation.surface: Breaks come when the bookmakers favour the specialists.
explanation.walkthrough: SP, starting price, is the British racing term for the final odds on a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaps or intervals between things, in time or place.

clue.text: Goes once better than the pursuing peelers

definitions.text: Goes once better than the pursuing peelers

parts.words: Goes once better than the pursuing peelers
parts.note: a fugitive who outruns the chasing police, peelers being an old British word for officers

explanation.surface: A fleeing suspect gets away from the police on his tail.
explanation.walkthrough: Peelers were early British policemen, named after Sir Robert Peel; the word also hints at stripping, a second play on the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave pursuers behind is to outdo or outpace them, exceeding rivals in speed.

clue.text: Hound of heaven worried these rulers

indicators.note: worried means shaken about, so the letters of the hound are disturbed

parts.note: Canis, the dog constellation such as Canis Major, is a hound in the sky

explanation.surface: Francis Thompson's divine pursuer bothered these monarchs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hound of heaven' recalls the poem but means Canis, the dog of the constellations; 'worried' turns CANIS into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inca emperors ruled a great Andean empire in Peru before the Spanish conquest.

clue.text: A pas de deux 17 featured bloomers like this

definitions.text: A pas de deux 17 featured bloomers like this

parts.words: A pas de deux 17 featured bloomers like this
parts.note: a dance for two performed on tiptoe recalls a flower whose name sounds like a pair of lips, as in tiptoeing through the flowers

explanation.surface: A ballet duet danced on tiptoe showed off flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 is ON POINTS, dancing on the tips of the toes; 'bloomers' are flowers, not underwear, and 'Tiptoe Through the Tulips' is the song behind the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A spring bulb flower with cup-shaped blooms, famously grown in the Netherlands.

clue.text: Actors often display it

indicators.note: display says the clue words put the answer on show within them

explanation.surface: Performers frequently show off their bodies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'display' shows the run inside 'acTORS Often', and the whole clue also describes what actors show.
explanation.definitionFit: The trunk of the human body, which actors may bare on stage.

clue.text: One chap came back holding a ring for the girl

indicators.note: holding means the word for chap encloses the ring
came back says the whole string runs backwards

parts.note: a chap is a man
O is shaped like a ring
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A man returned clutching a ring to give to his girlfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts O in MAN to make MOAN; I plus MOAN is then turned round by 'came back'.
explanation.definitionFit: Naomi is a girl's name, borne by Ruth's mother-in-law in the Bible.

clue.text: The value of warmth

parts.note: the phrase for the heat a fuel or food yields describes this word followed by value

explanation.surface: Someone praises the worth of being warm.
explanation.walkthrough: The heat energy in a food or fuel is called its calorific value.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means heat-producing, and goes with value for a measure of heat energy.

clue.text: Account of uncertainty ?

parts.note: an accounting term for a ledger holding doubtful items, read also as a story full of anxious waiting

explanation.surface: Someone tells a tale of doubt.
explanation.walkthrough: In bookkeeping a suspense account holds entries whose proper place is not yet settled; the word itself means anxious uncertainty.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means anxious uncertainty, and in bookkeeping names an account for unresolved items.

clue.text: Controllers of knobs

explanation.surface: Managers are described as door handles.
explanation.definitionFit: Managers who run things are their chiefs, and raised studs or knobs on a surface are also so called.
